nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$ with $y \neq 0$. Then $f(y)$ is an eigenvalue of the linear operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$.
nodes.title: $f(y)$ is an eigenvalue of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$. If some $w \in E$ with $w \neq 0$ satisfies $f(w) = 0$, then $0$ is an eigenvalue of the linear operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$.
nodes.title: $0$ is an eigenvalue of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$ when $f$ has a nontrivial kernel

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$. If some $w \in E$ with $w \neq 0$ satisfies $f(w) = 0$, then $0$ lies in the spectrum of the bounded operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$.
nodes.title: $0$ lies in the spectrum of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$ when $f$ has a nontrivial kernel

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$ with $y \neq 0$. Then $f(y)$ lies in the spectrum of the bounded operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$.
nodes.title: $f(y)$ lies in the spectrum of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, let $y \in E$, and let $T$ be the bounded operator on $E$ given by $T x = f(x)\,y$. If $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ satisfies $\mu \neq 0$ and $\mu \neq f(y)$, then $\mu$ is not in the spectrum of $T$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $E$.
nodes.title: The spectrum of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$ lies in $\{0, f(y)\}$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, let $y \in E$, and let $T$ be the bounded operator on $E$ given by $T x = f(x)\,y$. Then $T^2 = f(y)\,T$.
nodes.title: Square of the operator $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $H$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K}$ whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is linear in the second argument, let $x, y \in H$ with $x \neq 0$, and let $T$ be the bounded operator on $H$ given by $T z = \langle y, z \rangle\,x$. If some $w \in H$ with $w \neq 0$ satisfies $\langle y, w \rangle = 0$, then the spectrum of $T$ is…
nodes.title: Spectrum of the operator $z \mapsto \langle y, z \rangle\,x$ on a Hilbert space

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$ with $y \neq 0$ and $f(y) = 0$. Then the spectrum of the bounded operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$ is $\{0\}$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$ when $f(y) = 0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K}$, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional, and let $y \in E$ with $y \neq 0$. If some $w \in E$ with $w \neq 0$ satisfies $f(w) = 0$, then the spectrum of the bounded operator $T x = f(x)\,y$ on $E$ is exactly $\{0, f(y)\}$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of the operator $x \mapsto f(x)\,y$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
